documents.t: The Effects card is a composite card grouping three visual effects: Shadow, Glow and Edge.

A directional drop shadow that extends outward from the shape. Property Description Default Vertical Shadow direction on the vertical axis: None, Top, Bottom None Horizontal Shadow direction on the horizontal axis: None, Left, Right None Same as shape color Use the shape's primary color as the shadow color On Color Shadow color (visible only when Same as shape color is off) #000000 Transparency Shadow opacity (0–100%) 50 Size (px) Shadow extent in pixels (1–50) 5 The shadow is composed via SVG filters. The Vertical × Horizontal combination determines the offset direction: Vertical Horizontal Effect Top Left Shadow extends up-left Top Right Shadow extends up-right Bottom Left Shadow extends down-left Bottom Right Shadow extends down-right Bottom None Pure vertical shadow downward None Right Pure horizontal shadow rightward None None No shadow Unified fitting Shadow extension is integrated into the unified bounding box calculation: the shape is automatically scaled down to leave room for the shadow on the appropriate side. The shadow never bleeds back through the shape and never overflows the viewport. Taken over by the In/out button Turning on In/out button in the Button Mode card greys this group out. The shadow is then driven by the button position — outset while Off, inset while On — and uses its own fixed settings rather than the ones above.

A soft halo around the shape. Property Description Default Same as shape color Use the shape's primary color as the glow color On Color Glow color (visible only when Same as shape color is off) #FFFFFF Size (px) Glow radius in pixels (0–50) 0 Set Size to 0 to disable the glow.

Property Description Default Soften (px) Gaussian blur radius applied to the shape edge (0–20) 0 Edge softening creates a feathered border effect — useful for blending the tile into a colored background.
The Layout card controls how the Value and Label text blocks are positioned inside the tile. It is a composite card with three groups: Mode, Auto and Custom.

Property Description Default Custom positioning Toggle between automatic alignment and free positioning Off When Custom positioning is off, the Auto group is visible and controls the layout. When it is on, only the Custom group is visible.

Used when Custom positioning is off. Power BI's standard alignment behaviour applies. Property Description Default Alignment Horizontal alignment (Left / Center / Right) Center Vertical Alignment Vertical alignment (Top / Middle / Bottom) Middle Spacing Gap (px) between the value and the label 0 Label under Value When on, the label is placed below the value; otherwise the renderer chooses based on alignment Off

Used when Custom positioning is on. Each text block is positioned by an X/Y percentage relative to the inscribed bounding box of the shape. Property Description Default Label X (%) Horizontal position of the label center (0 = left, 100 = right). -1 = unset. -1 Label Y (%) Vertical position of the label center (0 = top, 100 = bottom). -1 = unset. -1 Value X (%) Horizontal position of the value center -1 Value Y (%) Vertical position of the value center -1

You don't have to type X/Y values manually. In edit mode, simply click and drag the value or label inside the tile: The first drag automatically switches Mode → Custom positioning to on The dragged block's X/Y is persisted via Power BI's persistProperties API Subsequent renders use the saved coordinates To go back to automatic centering, switch Custom positioning back to off. The X/Y values are kept but ignored. Mixing modes The Auto/Custom switch is global to all text blocks. If you want only one of them to be custom, drag both — but set the other one's X/Y to a value matching the auto position.

Property Description Default Do not print or export The tile renders nothing when the report is exported or printed Off Intended for tiles that are report chrome rather than content — a navigation or filter button, a decorative shape — and have no place in a PDF or a printout. It is the other half of the transparent overlay technique: native buttons are already excluded from print and export, so turning this on makes the custom-looking control disappear as a whole. Two different paths reach a printed page, and both are covered: Server-side exports (Export to PDF, PowerPoint, image, and e-mail subscriptions) run the visual in Power BI's export host. The visual detects it through hostEnv and renders nothing, while still signalling renderingFinished so the export does not stall. The browser's own Print renders the visual normally, so the tile is additionally hidden by an @media print rule. The tile keeps behaving normally on screen — only the printed and exported output is affected.
The Logo card controls the size and position of the image bound to the Logo data role.

Property Description Default Width (px) Logo width in pixels (0–500). 0 = follow the height at the image's own aspect ratio 40 Height (px) Logo height in pixels (0–500). 0 = follow the width at the image's own aspect ratio 40 X (%) Horizontal center position (0 = left, 100 = right) 50 Y (%) Vertical center position (0 = top, 100 = bottom) 50

Width and Height are independent, and a 0 means derive me from the other one: Width Height Result 40 40 Exactly 40×40 — the image is stretched to fit, aspect ratio ignored 40 0 40 px wide, height computed from the image's proportions 0 40 40 px tall, width computed from the image's proportions 0 0 The image's own natural size The proportional modes need the image's intrinsic dimensions, which the visual measures once per image and caches. On the very first render of a new image the logo is drawn as a 40 px square, then redrawn at the correct ratio as soon as the measurement lands — a flicker you may notice when swapping images while authoring. SVG logos An SVG without an intrinsic size reports no natural dimensions. Such an image keeps the 40 px square fallback in the proportional modes — give it an explicit Width and Height instead.

The logo position is always custom — there is no auto-alignment for the logo. In edit mode you can drag the logo anywhere inside the tile: Click and drag the logo The new X/Y is persisted via persistProperties Subsequent renders use the saved position

The logo is rendered as an SVG <image> element layered behind the value and label text blocks. It only appears when: The Logo or Logo (active) data role is bound to a measure, and The measure returns a non-empty value (a base64 string or a data:image/...;base64,... URI) If the value does not start with data:, the visual automatically prepends data:image/png;base64,.

When the tile is used as a Button Mode button, Logo is shown while the button is Off and Logo (active) while it is On. This card sizes and positions both — they share the same box, so the two images stay in place as the button flips.

For icon-style logos (brand marks, status icons), 32×32 to 64×64 px is usually enough Leave one dimension at 0 rather than matching the two by hand: the image then keeps its proportions whatever you replace it with Keep base64 source images small (under 5 KB) to avoid bloating the data model See Data Roles → Logo for guidance on preparing base64 images.
The Prefix Label card adds an optional short text that appears in front of the value — typically a currency symbol, a unit or a signed indicator.

Property Description Default Show (toggle) Master switch — shows or hides the prefix Off Text Prefix text displayed before the value (e.g. $, €, ≈, +) (empty) End Spacing Extra gap (px) between the prefix and the value (0–50) 4 Font Color Prefix text color. Supports conditional formatting (fx). #FFFFFF Font Font family, size, bold, italic, underline (FontControl) Segoe UI, 16 px

Currency symbol — $, €, £ before the value when the measure format string does not already include one Units — ≈, ~, ± to express approximations or tolerances Trend indicator — ↑ or ↓ driven by a conditional format rule based on variation

The prefix is anchored to the left of the value and follows the value's position. When the value is dragged or repositioned through the Layout card, the prefix follows. The End Spacing property controls how much horizontal room is left between the end of the prefix and the first character of the value. Increase it for an airier look, decrease to 0 for a tight composition.
The prefix uses its own FontControl, independent from the value. This lets you combine, for example, a small $ prefix with a large bold value, or a light italic ≈ with a regular value.
The Shape card controls the geometric form of the tile, its fill color and an optional gradient.

Property Description Default Shape Geometry of the tile (17 options — see below) Rectangle Trapezoid Angle Slope angle (°) — only when Shape is Trapezoid 75 From Color Primary fill color. Supports conditional formatting (fx). #4A6FA5 To Color Second color of the gradient. Supports conditional formatting (fx). #4A6FA5 Gradient Direction of the linear gradient: None, Horizontal →, Vertical ↓, Diagonal ↘, Diagonal ↗ None Transparency Fill opacity (0–100%). Supports conditional formatting (fx). 0

Shape Notes Rectangle 4 corners — supports per-corner styling Circle Inscribed circle (no corners) Ellipse Elliptical fit to the container Diamond 4 corners — supports per-corner styling Triangle 3 corners — supports per-corner styling Pentagon Convex angles (inscribed circle fit) Hexagon Convex angles (inscribed circle fit) Octagon Convex angles (inscribed circle fit) Star (5) Convex + reflex angles Star (6) Convex + reflex angles Arrow Convex + reflex angles — use Mirror H/V + Rotation for direction Chevron Convex + reflex angles — use Mirror H/V + Rotation for direction Parallelogram 4 corners Trapezoid 4 corners + Trapezoid Angle slider Cross Convex + reflex angles Heart No corners (curved path) Pill No corners (rounded ends) Single-direction shapes Triangle, arrow and chevron come in a single canonical orientation. To get other variants (down-arrow, left-chevron, etc.) combine Mirror Horizontal, Mirror Vertical and Rotation from the Transform card.

Pick two colors in From Color and To Color, then set Gradient to a direction other than None. The gradient is rendered as an SVG <linearGradient> filling the entire shape. Series Color overrides gradient When the Series Color data role is bound to a measure, the gradient is automatically forced to None and both colors are overridden by the data value. See Data Roles.

Transparency, From Color and To Color all expose the fx button. Use it to drive these properties from a measure or rule based on your data: TileColor = SWITCH( TRUE(), [KPI] >= [Target], "#2E8B57", [KPI] >= 0.8 * [Target], "#DAA520", "#B22222" )
The Transform card applies horizontal/vertical mirroring and free rotation to the shape.

Property Description Default Mirror Horizontal Flip the shape along its vertical axis Off Mirror Vertical Flip the shape along its horizontal axis Off Rotation (deg) Rotation angle, 0–360°. Supports conditional formatting (fx). 0 Rotate Text & Logo Rotate the text and the logo together with the shape. See below Off

By default only the shape rotates: the value, the label and the logo stay upright and readable. With Rotate Text & Logo on, the text and the logo are laid out in the shape's unrotated frame, then the whole content layer is rotated about the shape's center along with the shape — so a tile turned 90° carries vertical text. Mirroring never mirrors the text, which stays legible. The content follows live while the rotation handle is dragged.

The Triangle, Arrow and Chevron shapes are defined in a single canonical orientation (pointing right for arrow/chevron, pointing up for triangle). To get the other directions, combine mirroring and rotation: Desired direction Mirror H Mirror V Rotation Arrow → right — — 0° Arrow ← left Yes — 0° Arrow ↑ up — — 270° Arrow ↓ down — — 90° Triangle ▲ up — — 0° Triangle ▼ down — Yes 0°

In edit mode, hover the tile and a small rotation handle appears at the top of the shape. Drag it to rotate the tile in real time: The path's transform attribute is updated continuously during the drag for instant visual feedback On drop, the final angle is persisted via Power BI's persistProperties API The handle is hidden in view mode You can also type the exact rotation in the slider, or drive it from a measure with the fx button.
The Value card controls the formatting of the main numeric value displayed in the tile.

Property Description Default Font Color Color of the value text. Supports conditional formatting (fx). #FFFFFF Font Family Font family used for the value DIN Font Size Font size in pixels (4–200). Supports conditional formatting (fx). 27 Bold / Italic / Underline Standard text style toggles Off Display Units Auto, None, Thousands (K), Millions (M), Billions (bn), Trillions (T). Combined with the measure's format string. Auto Decimal Places Number of decimals (0–6). When 0, the measure's format string drives precision; any value greater than 0 overrides it. 0

Font Size supports conditional formatting (fx) — the size in pixels can be driven by a DAX measure. Use this when you want the visual to scale with the value (e.g. several MetricTile visuals on a page where the most important figure stands out by being larger). See Conditional font size — DAX recipes for ready-to-paste formulas.

The displayed value is built by combining the measure's format string (currency symbols, %, custom suffixes, locale separators) with the Display Units and Decimal Places set on this card. Tooltip and card share the same formatted output, so they always stay consistent. The format string is read from the bound measure's Format property in your model (e.g. "$#,0.00", "0.00%", "#,0"). The card then layers Display Units / Decimal Places on top.

Assuming the measure's format is "$#,0.00" (currency with two decimals): Value Display Units Decimal Places Output 123.29 Auto 1 $123.3 1,299 Auto 1 $1.3K 123,456,789 Auto 1 $123.5M 1,299 None 0 $1,299.00 (format string precision) 1,299 Thousands 2 $1.30K Auto picks the appropriate suffix from the value's magnitude (no scaling under 1,000; K from 1,000; M from 1,000,000; etc.). None disables scaling entirely. Decimal Places = 0 means « use the format string's natural precision »; any value greater than 0 overrides it. If you need a per-locale or per-context format (e.g. € instead of $), edit the measure's Format in your model — the card and the tooltip will both follow.

The value is centered horizontally and vertically by default, using a scan-line intersection algorithm: the renderer projects horizontal scan lines through the inscribed bounding box of the (possibly rotated) shape and picks the largest unobstructed band, ensuring the text never overflows the silhouette — even for diamond, triangle, star, heart and other non-rectangular shapes. To override the automatic centering, use the Layout card with Custom positioning on, or simply drag the value text in edit mode.

The MetricTile visual accepts seven data roles — one Grouping and six Measures. Only Value is mandatory; the others enrich the tile when present. Data Role Type Description Category Grouping Optional grouping column (e.g. Planet.Label). Provides row context for measures and serves as a default label when no Label measure is bound. Value Measure The numeric value displayed in the center of the tile Label Measure The descriptive label (overrides the Category value and the static text in the Category Label card) Series Color Measure A hex color code (e.g. #FF0000) — overrides the shape From color and disables gradient Logo Measure A base64-encoded image rendered inside the tile Logo (active) Measure A second base64-encoded image, shown while a Button Mode button is in its On position Tooltips Measure Extra measures shown only in the tooltip when hovering the tile Single-row visual The MetricTile is designed to display a single value. The dataView is read with value.max = 1, label.max = 1, etc. Aggregate your data so each visual instance returns one row per role.

The Category data role is the only Grouping role on the visual. It provides row context for the measures (so they evaluate in the current filter + category) and acts as a default label when no Label measure is bound. Bind a column — typically a dimension key like Planet.Label or Product.Name — and the visual will read its first value as the tile label.

Drag any measure into Value. The visual respects the format string of the underlying measure (currency symbol, percentage, decimals…) but you can override formatting from the Value formatting card (display units, decimal places).

The Label data role lets you build a dynamic descriptive label from DAX. For example: TileLabel = "Sales — " & SELECTEDVALUE('Calendar'[Year]) The label text is resolved with the following priority (first non-empty wins): Label measure (dynamic, highest priority) Category value (from the Grouping role) Text field in the Category Label formatting card (static) Name of the bound Value measure (last-resort fallback)

Use a measure that returns a hex color string to drive the tile color from your data model. Common patterns: StatusColor = VAR pct = DIVIDE([Actual], [Target]) RETURN SWITCH( TRUE(), pct >= 1, "#2E8B57", // green pct >= 0.8, "#DAA520", // amber "#B22222" // red ) When Series Color is bound, the gradient direction is forced to None and both From and To colors are overridden by the data value. Hex format only Colors must be valid hex codes (#RGB or #RRGGBB). Color names like red and rgb(...) notations are not supported.

The Logo data role accepts base64-encoded images. If the value does not start with data:, the visual automatically prepends data:image/png;base64,. The logo appears as an <image> element layered behind the value/label text. Its size and position are controlled by the Logo formatting card, and it can be dragged in edit mode just like the text blocks. Image size Keep your base64 logos small (under 5 KB, typically 32×32 to 64×64 px). Large images bloat the data model and slow down Power BI.

Logo (active) is a second image, used when the tile acts as a two-position button: Logo is shown while the button is Off, Logo (active) while it is On. Either role may be left empty — a single logo is then used in both positions. Outside Button Mode, only Logo is used.
Conditional formatting (fx) — rules set in the formatting cards Series Color / Logo data roles — values from your data model Static values — colors and settings entered in the formatting pane

Open the Format pane and try these: Shape → Shape — pick another shape (circle, hexagon, star, pill…) Shape → From / To Color + Gradient — apply a two-color gradient Effects → Shadow — add a drop shadow with direction and size Corners → Top Left / Top Right / … — switch corners between rounded and right-angled Transform → Rotation — rotate the tile (a drag handle also appears in edit mode on hover)

The SDM MetricTile is a custom Power BI visual that displays a single numeric metric inside a richly customizable shape tile. It is designed as a flexible alternative to Power BI's built-in card visual, with full control over shape, color, gradient, effects, typography and positioning.

Feature Description 17 shapes Rectangle, circle, ellipse, diamond, triangle, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, 5-point star, 6-point star, arrow, chevron, parallelogram, trapezoid, cross, heart, pill Linear gradients Two-color gradients in horizontal, vertical or diagonal directions Per-corner styling Right-angled, rounded, or inward variants on each corner of multi-vertex shapes Mirror & rotation Horizontal/vertical mirror and 0–360° rotation, with live drag handle in edit mode Effects Drop shadow (directional, with size/transparency), glow, edge softening Drag positioning Value, label and logo can be dragged anywhere in edit mode Data-driven color Override the shape color from a measure returning a hex code Data-driven logo Embed a base64 image in the tile from a measure Conditional formatting Most properties (colors, transparency, font sizes, rotation, corner radius) support fx rules Prefix label Optional text prefix in front of the value (currency, units…) Category label Optional descriptive label below or beside the value Button Mode The tile becomes a two-position button that cross-filters the page (on its Category, and/or with a Filter JSON per position), with an in/out look and a logo per position — see Button Mode Rotate text with the shape Optionally rotate the text and logo along with the shape Entrance animation Fade, Grow or Cascade, replayed only when the data changes — see Animation Licensing & watermark Free / Pro plans, watermark removed with a valid key
Feature Free Pro All shapes & effects Yes Yes Data-driven color & logo Yes Yes Drag positioning Yes Yes Conditional formatting Yes Yes Watermark Shown Hidden Support Community Email

The MetricTile is built for dashboard headline metrics — KPIs, counters, totals, scorecards — where the visual identity matters and a plain card looks too sterile. Typical scenarios: KPI tiles with brand-coloured backgrounds and logos Status badges driven by conditional formatting (red/green/amber on threshold) Star ratings, arrows, chevrons used for sentiment or direction Pills and rounded rectangles in modern dashboard layouts

The Animation card plays a short entrance animation when the cloud appears or when its data changes.

Property Description Default Animation (card toggle) Turns the entrance animation on or off On Type Fade: the whole visual fades in. Grow: the words are drawn first, then the details fade in. Cascade: a staggered variant of Grow Grow Duration (ms) Duration of the main animation, 100–5000 ms 800

The animation is an entrance: the cloud is redrawn from scratch on every update. It is only replayed when the data changes, and skipped for: a resize, a click in the Format pane, a selection or a live search — anything that leaves the data untouched; an export (PDF, PowerPoint, image, subscriptions); viewers whose operating system asks for reduced motion.
documents.s: When it plays — and when it does not

documents.t: The Background card pours the cloud into a silhouette: a preset shape or the shape of an image you provide. With None, the cloud simply fills the rectangle of the visual.

Property Description Default Shape None (rectangular cloud), Circle, Square, Diamond, Triangle, Pentagon, Star, Cardioid or Custom image mask None Image (base64) The image used as mask and drawn behind the words when Shape is Custom image mask. Supports fx, so it can come from a measure (empty) Image opacity (%) Opacity of the image drawn behind the words, 0–100 25 Ellipticity Width / height stretch of a preset shape (ignored for an image mask) 1 Respect rotation See below Off Shrink to fit Shrinks a word toward Layout → Min font size before giving up on placing it On Grid resolution (px) Precision of the placement grid. Smaller = denser and more precise, larger = faster 4 Time budget (ms) Placement stops and draws whatever fits once this budget is exceeded 3000

Paste a base64-encoded image into Image (base64). The non-transparent part of the image is where words may be placed; the image itself is drawn behind the cloud at the chosen opacity. A logo or a country outline with a transparent background works best. The image is sanitized before use and is never injected as HTML.

By default words stay horizontal in shape mode, which is fast and robust. Turning Respect rotation on honors Layout → Rotation but makes every collision check slower, so the cloud may need a larger time budget.

If a very large cloud takes longer than the Time budget, placement stops and the words that already fit are drawn. Words that did not fit are left out; raise the budget, lower Max words, lower the grid precision (larger value) or turn Shrink to fit on to include more of them.
The Colors card sets how words are colored when no other rule takes over.

Property Description Default Mode Single color, Categorical palette, Gradient by value or Series Color measure Categorical palette Color The color of every word in Single color mode (also the fallback in Series Color measure mode) #2C6FBB From Color of the smallest value in Gradient by value mode #2C6FBB To Color of the largest value in Gradient by value mode #E63946

Colors from this card are the last in the priority order: a Series Color measure value for the word; the Significance colors, as soon as a test is selected; this card. So while a significance test is on, the Colors card has no visible effect; set Significance → Test to None to see it again.
The Filtering card is a composite card with two groups: Limits and Live search.

Property Description Default Max words Number of words kept, largest values first 100 Minimum value Words whose (merged) value is below this are dropped 0 Stop words Comma-separated words excluded from the cloud (case-insensitive), e.g. the, and, a, of (empty)

An optional search box to find words in the cloud. The search is client-side only: nothing is saved with the report, and the text is kept until the page is reloaded. Property Description Default Show search box Displays the box on the visual Off Search box location Top or Bottom of the visual Top Show on hover On: the box floats over the cloud and appears when the pointer is over the visual (in design and reading modes). Off: the box is always visible and reserves its own strip, so it never covers the words Off Default behavior Initial behavior of the search: Highlight, Select or Filter (see below) Filter Placeholder Hint text of the empty box Search words… Font size Size of the typed text 12 Font color Color of the typed text #333333 Background Background color of the box #ffffff

Icon Behavior Effect 💡 Light bulb Highlight Matching words stay lit, the others are dimmed (same opacity as unselected words, see Selection) ➤ Arrow Select Same as Highlight, and the matching words are selected: the other visuals of the page are cross-filtered, as if you had clicked the words. Clearing the search clears the selection ⛛ Funnel Filter Only the matching words are drawn, and the cloud is laid out again The box ends with these three buttons, so the end-user can switch behavior on the fly. Only one is active at a time. Default behavior is the starting choice; if you change it in the Format pane, any choice made by the viewer is reset. A fourth button, ?, opens a help window (in the language of the user) that explains the icons and gives a few regular-expression tips.

The text typed is a regular expression, matched anywhere in the word and ignoring case. Pattern Matches paris|lyon "paris" or "lyon" — the way to filter on two names ^data words starting with "data" ing$ words ending with "ing" ^(paris|lyon)$ exactly "paris" or exactly "lyon" colou?r "color" or "colour" (? makes the previous letter optional) a.*z "a", then anything, then "z" An incomplete pattern (for example an unclosed parenthesis while typing) is searched as plain text, so no error is shown.
The Layout card controls the typography and the placement of the words.

Property Description Default Font Font family of the words Segoe UI Min font size Size of the smallest word (at least 4) 12 Max font size Size of the largest word 80 Size scale How a value maps to a size: Linear, Square root or Logarithmic Square root Rotation Horizontal only, Horizontal + Vertical, or Free angles Horizontal + Vertical Spacing Padding around each word, in pixels 2 Spiral Archimedean or Rectangular search path used to find a free spot Archimedean Random seed Seeds the random choices of the layout (word rotation, starting positions). The same seed gives the same cloud on every reload; 0 gives a new random cloud each time 1

Linear keeps the proportions of the data but lets one dominant word crush the others. Square root is a good compromise and the default. Logarithmic flattens strong differences — useful when the top words are far above the rest. Reproducible layout The cloud uses random choices (word rotation, starting positions). With the default Random seed of 1 the layout is identical on every reload. Change the number to get another arrangement you like, or set 0 for a different one each time. The layout still depends on the data order, the font and the size of the visual. Shape and mask mode When a Background shape or image mask is selected, the words are placed by a different engine: Spiral does not apply, and Rotation is only honored when Respect rotation is on.
Clicking a word selects it and cross-filters the other visuals of the page (Ctrl / ⌘ + click adds to the selection, a click elsewhere clears it).

Property Description Default Unselected opacity (%) Opacity of the words that are not selected, 0–100 30 Selections follow the report's Edit interactions settings; where interactions are switched off, clicks and the context menu are inert.
The Significance card decides which words are significantly more or less frequent than a reference, and how they are highlighted.

Property Description Default Test None, Vs global average or Vs comparison measure — see below None Confidence level 90%, 95% or 99% 95% Variance Pooled or Separate — see Variance Separate Minimum base Words whose Base is below this are never flagged 30 Above reference Color of a word significantly above the reference #cc0000 Below reference Color of a word significantly below the reference #007700 Not significant Color of every other word #888888 Highlight style Color only, Color + Bold or Color + Outline (a significant word only) Color + Bold
Both are a two-proportion z-test: z = (p1 − p2) / √variance, where p1 = Value / Base for the word.

The reference is the rest of the cloud: p2 = (total Value − word Value) / (total Base − word Base). The word is left out of its own reference, so it is never compared against a total that contains itself. The totals are computed on all the words that remain after cleaning, before Max words is applied. Needs Base.

The reference is the word's own p2 = Comparison / Comparison Base: last period, another segment, a benchmark. Needs Base, Comparison and Comparison Base. In both modes the word stays Not significant when its Base is below Minimum base or when the reference base is zero.

The two methods give close results when the bases are similar and the proportions not extreme. Method Variance Reads as Separate (default) p1(1−p1)/n1 + p2(1−p2)/n2 Each proportion keeps its own variance Pooled p(1−p)(1/n1 + 1/n2), with p the pooled proportion Variance under the hypothesis that both proportions are equal
As soon as Test is not None, every word takes one of the three significance colors, whatever the Colors card says. Only a Series Color measure can still override them.
documents.s: Colors while a test is on

documents.t: The Words card cleans the text of the Words column before anything is counted.

Property Description Default Case As-is, lowercase, UPPERCASE or Capitalize (first letter upper, the rest lower) As-is Combine duplicates by How Value is combined when the same word appears on several rows: Sum, Count (number of rows) or Average Sum Minimum length Words shorter than this number of characters are dropped 1

Normalizing the case makes Price, price and PRICE the same text. The rows are then merged into a single word: Value, Base, Comparison and Comparison Base are summed over the merged rows (for Sum and, once converted, Average); with Count the word's value becomes the number of rows merged; with Average, the sum divided by that number; the first row's selection identity, Series Color and tooltip are kept.
documents.s: Why Case and Combine duplicates go together

documents.t: Case and trimming Minimum length and stop words Merging of duplicates Minimum value Significance tests — on the whole remaining set, so a word's flag does not change when you change Max words Max words: the words with the largest values are kept

Data Role Type Description Words Grouping Categorical text column — one row per word or phrase to draw Value Measure Sizes the word (frequency, mentions, score…) Base Measure Sample size behind Value. Required by both significance modes Comparison Measure Reference value per word (e.g. previous period). Used by the Vs comparison measure mode Comparison Base Measure Sample size behind Comparison Series Color Measure A hex color code (e.g. #FF0000) that overrides every other color for that word Tooltips Measure Extra measures shown only in the tooltip Only Words and Value are needed to draw a cloud; the others are optional. Row limit The visual reads at most the first 500 rows of the Words column. Use the Filtering card (or a Top N filter on the field) to keep the words that matter.

The significance test compares proportions. For a word, p = Value / Base: Value is the number of observations that mention the word, Base the number of observations the proportion is computed on (for instance the number of respondents). Bind counts, not already-computed percentages.
documents.s: Value and Base: counts, not percentages

documents.t: In Vs comparison measure mode each word is tested against its own reference: p1 = Value / Base against p2 = Comparison / Comparison Base. Both bases must be bound and positive, otherwise the word stays neutral.

When several rules could color a word, the first that applies wins: Series Color measure, when the word has a value; the significance colors (above / below / not significant), as soon as a test is selected; the Colors card (single, palette, gradient).
Hovering a word shows its text, its Value, its Base, Comparison and Comparison Base when bound, followed by every measure placed in Tooltips. Report-page tooltips are supported.

The SDM WordCloud is a custom Power BI visual that turns a text column into a word cloud — and goes one step further: it tests which words are statistically over- or under-represented and highlights them, so the cloud reports a finding instead of just drawing a shape.

Feature Description Significance highlighting Each word is tested with a two-proportion z-test, either against the global average of the cloud or against a comparison measure (last period, another segment, a benchmark), at a 90/95/99% confidence level — see Significance Minimum base A word whose base is below a threshold is never flagged, so small samples don't produce noisy results Three highlight styles Color only, color + bold, or color + outline, with distinct above / below / neutral colors Shapes and image masks Seven preset silhouettes (circle, square, diamond, triangle, pentagon, star, cardioid) or a plain rectangle, plus a custom image mask from a base64 image — see Background Size scale Linear, square-root or logarithmic, with adjustable min and max font size and spacing Rotation Horizontal only, horizontal + vertical, or free angles; Archimedean or rectangular spiral Never freezes A configurable time budget: placement stops and draws what fits on a very large cloud Cleaning Case normalization, merging of duplicates by sum / count / average, stop words, minimum length — see Words and Filtering Limits Maximum number of words and minimum value Live search An optional search box (regular expressions) with three behaviors the viewer can switch: highlight, select (cross-filter the page) or filter the cloud Colors Single color, categorical palette, gradient by value, or a Series Color measure driving each word Report interactivity Click a word to cross-filter the page, hover for a tooltip, right-click for the Power BI menu — see Interactivity Entrance animation Fade, Grow or Cascade, replayed only when the data changes — see Animation Localization Format pane localized in 10 languages Licensing & watermark Free / Pro plans, watermark removed with a valid key
